questions.question: How does the mechanic or pilot control or steer the aircraft while on the ground?
questions.idealAnswer: Control of steering is from the flight deck through the use of a small wheel, tiller, or joy stick.

concepts.label: Control of steering is from the flight deck through the use of a small wheel

questions.question: How are shock struts measured?
questions.idealAnswer: The correct amount of inflation is measured in psi on some struts. Other manufactures specify struts to be inflated until extension of the lower strut is a certain measurement. Always follow the manufacture's instructions.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a locking/disconnect pin on a nose gear strut?
questions.idealAnswer: To disconnect steering when the aircraft is being towed or positioned in place.

questions.question: What is used to power large aircraft nose wheel steering?
questions.idealAnswer: Hydraulics power predominates.

questions.question: What device is designed to prevent accidental gear retraction while the aircraft is on the ground?
questions.idealAnswer: A landing gear squat switch, weight on wheels switch, or a safety switch is used on most aircraft.

concepts.label: or a safety switch is used on most aircraft
terms: or a safety switch is used on most aircraft

questions.question: What should be done if a properly operating fusible plug has allowed an aircraft tire to deflate.
questions.idealAnswer: Fusible plugs or thermal plugs must be inspected visually. A close inspection should reveal whether any core has experienced deformation that might be due to high temperature. If detected all thermal plugs in the wheel should be replaced with new.

questions.question: Prior to performing an inspection on the landing gear group, how should the mechanic prepare the area?
questions.idealAnswer: All surfaces should be clean to ensure that no trouble spots are undetected.

questions.question: How can you detect wear on a break assembly?
questions.idealAnswer: Many brake assemblies contain a built- in indicator wear pin, Typically, the exposed pin length decreases as the linings wear, and a minimum length is used to determine when the linings must be replaced. On small aircraft a measurement is taking directly from the brake linings and checked against the aircraft maintenance manual directions.

questions.question: If the pilot reports that the brakes feel spongy, what might the cause be?
questions.idealAnswer: The presence of air in the brake system fluid causes the brake pedal to feel spongy.

questions.question: What is the usual repair for a pilot discrepancy that the brakes feel spongy?
questions.idealAnswer: Trapped air in the lines can be removed by bleeding the breaks to restore firm brake pedal feel.

questions.question: How are the typical modern two-piece wheel constructed?
questions.idealAnswer: They are either cast or forged from aluminum or magnesium alloy.

questions.question: How long can brake linings remain in service?
questions.idealAnswer: Brake linings can remain in service until they exceed the individual manufacturer's wear specifications.

questions.question: Explain the phrase ("bleeding the brakes").
questions.idealAnswer: Bleeding the brakes is a maintenance procedure that removes trapped air in the hydraulic fluid in the brakes. Fluid is bled from the brake system until their is an absence of air bubbles.

questions.question: How can it be determined that all air has been purged from a master cylinder brake system?
questions.idealAnswer: After bleeding the brakes, operate the brakes and note their feel; Firm brakes have had the air properly removed, if they feel spongy air is still in the system.

questions.question: What should you look for when inspecting bearings?
questions.idealAnswer: Defects that would render it unserviceable, such as cracks, flaking, broken baring surfaces, roughness due to impact pressure or surface wear, corrosion or pitting, discoloration from excessive heat, cracked or broken barring cages, and scored or loose barring cups or or cones that would affect proper seating on the axel or wheel.

questions.question: How should tires be stored?
questions.idealAnswer: They should always be stored vertically so that it is resting on its treaded surface. Storage of tires on a tire rack with a minimum 3-4 - inch flat resting surface for the tread is ideal and avoids tire distortion.

questions.question: What does excessive wear in the center of the tread on an aircraft tire indicate?
questions.idealAnswer: The tire has been over inflated.

questions.question: How does over inflation affect tire life?
questions.idealAnswer: It leads to premature tread wear, reducing the number of cycles in service before a tire must be replaced. It makes a tire more susceptible to bruising, cutting, shock damage, and blow out.

questions.question: How is a wheel skid detected by an anti- skid system.
questions.idealAnswer: Wheel speed sensors are located on each wheel equipped with a brake assembly.

questions.question: How is the anti-skid braking system generally armed by the pilot?

questions.question: Explain the general operation of the landing gear warning system.
questions.idealAnswer: A system of lights used to indicate the condition of the landing gear. A red light illuminates when any of the gears are in an unsafe condition; a green light shows when all gear is down and locked, and no light when gear is up and locked. An aural warning system is installed that sounds a horn if any of the landing gears are not down and locked when throttles are retarded for landing.

questions.idealAnswer: They should be properly inflated.

questions.question: What kind of bolts are used in landing gear?
questions.idealAnswer: Steel bolts are used.

questions.question: What takes up the shock of the landing impact in an oleo shock strut?
questions.idealAnswer: The metered transfer of hydraulic fluid through an orifice from the lower chamber to upper chamber of the shock strut.

questions.question: What takes up the taxi shocks in an oleo shock strut?
questions.idealAnswer: Compressed air (or nitrogen) in the upper chamber.

questions.question: How much oil should be put into an oleo shock strut?

questions.question: What is the purpose of the centering cam in a nosewheel shock strut?
questions.idealAnswer: The centering cam straightens the nosewheel with the strut before retracting gear into nose gear well.

questions.question: How does a shimmy damper keep a nosewheel from shimmying?
questions.idealAnswer: The shimmy damper functions as a hydraulic shock absorber between the piston and cylinder of the nosewheel shock strut. It transfers fluid between two chamber (via) a small hole in the piston.

questions.idealAnswer: The compensator port opens the brake reservoir to the wheel cylinders when brakes are released, preventing pressure buildup in brake lines, which prevents brake drag when caliper remains engaged and there is slow or no release from rotor.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the shuttle valve in the brake system of an aircraft using hydraulic power brakes?
questions.idealAnswer: The shuttle valve is an automatic transfer valve which allows main hydraulic system pressure for brake operation under normal conditions, but, if main system pressure is lost, it allows fluid in from the emergency backup system for brake operation.

questions.question: Why are fusible plugs installed on some aircraft wheels?
questions.idealAnswer: It releases pressure generated by heat buildup before a tire blows.

questions.question: What safety precaution must be taken when removing a wheel from an axle or disassembling a wheel?
questions.idealAnswer: Be sure to completely deflate the tire.

questions.question: What is the name of the unit that prevents a nose wheel from vibrating or oscillating?

questions.question: What are the most common sources of power used to extend and retract landing gear?
questions.idealAnswer: Hydraulic pressure and electric motors.

questions.question: At what times should a gear retraction check be performed?
questions.idealAnswer: During annuals or other inspections, removal and replacement, or following hard landings.

questions.question: Name several types of brake actuating systems.

questions.question: What is the function of an anti-skid system?
